name: Port-la-Nouvelle
title: Port-la-Nouvelle Gauging | UTM for Bulkers & Wind-Port Vessels
description: Thickness measurement at Port-la-Nouvelle for grain and fertiliser bulkers, product tankers, offshore wind support vessels and coasters: UTM on hulls and tanks.
h1: Ship Thickness Gauging at Port-la-Nouvelle, Occitanie
intro: Port-la-Nouvelle sits on the Languedoc coast between Narbonne and Perpignan. It is a working bulk port for grain, fertiliser and liquid products, and has recently added a large offshore wind terminal for floating wind turbines. Gauging is requested for bulk carriers, tankers, coasters and the support vessels that follow wind projects. The inspection team travels from India to join the ship, as there is no base along this part of the Mediterranean coast.

highlights.p: The extended port was developed to assemble floating wind turbines. Installation, tug and support vessels call for work on hull, deck and ballast steel before or after a campaign.
Handysize bulk carriers load and discharge farm products here. The gap between discharge and loading is the usual window for hold frame and tank top gauging.
A compact harbour with one main channel means ships berth quickly and the agent can arrange access without the queues of a major hub, which suits a short gauging call.

p: Port-la-Nouvelle is a deep-water port on the Aude coast, sheltered behind breakwaters and fronting the open Gulf of Lion. It is run by the Occitanie regional authority under the Port Occitanie brand, alongside its sister port at Sète. The port has a fishing harbour, commercial basins and a long outer quay area, and in recent years the harbour has been enlarged to open up a new deep-water platform. A canal links the harbour to the lagoons inland, but ship traffic passes through the harbour mouth only.

Cargo is a mix of dry and liquid bulk. Grain and oilseed from the local plains leave by sea, fertiliser and agricultural inputs arrive, and hydrocarbon and other liquid products are stored in tanks near the quays and loaded or discharged by small tankers. Wine and local products add a minor flow. The newer element is the offshore wind platform, developed to assemble floating turbines and to base the tugs and support vessels used to tow them out to farms planned off this coast. Ship size is moderate, with handysize bulk carriers, small tankers and coasters the usual callers.

Weather defines the work. The tramontane blows from the north-west with force, and onshore swell can build quickly during autumn and winter depressions. Pilots may delay entries and departures, and quay-side work is not always comfortable in strong wind. Gauging plans for ships waiting outside the breakwater carry a wide weather allowance, and the preference is to work alongside once the ship has berthed. Quieter months are late spring and summer, when sea conditions are more settled and the offshore support fleet is most active.

facilities.h: Where ships can be gauged at Port-la-Nouvelle
p: Nearly all gauging happens alongside. Bulk quays take grain and fertiliser ships, and the agent arranges gate passes so that technicians reach the berth. Hold frames and tank tops are accessible between discharge and loading, with ballast tanks and void spaces readable whenever the ship releases them. The liquid bulk berths follow terminal safety rules, so work in tanks goes ahead only with the ship's enclosed-space permit and the terminal's agreement.

The new wind platform is a large quayside area designed for assembly and loading, and support vessels may lie there for weeks between tasks, which makes it a useful place for planned gauging. The port's repair capacity is modest, with small slipways and quayside repair for fishing craft and workboats. A merchant ship due a dry docking normally heads for Marseille, La Ciotat or Barcelona, and Port-la-Nouvelle then becomes the pre-docking call where gauging helps scope steel renewal.
list: Commercial bulk quays, for hold frame, hopper tank and hatch coaming gauging on grain and fertiliser ships.
Liquid bulk berths, for ballast tank and deck gauging on small tankers within terminal permit rules.
Offshore wind platform quays, for hull, deck and ballast steel on tugs and support vessels during stand-by.
Fishing harbour berths, for trawler hull and tank gauging during lay-up.
Slipway and small repair quay, for workboats and fishing craft only.
Roads outside the breakwater, for launch-served work in calm weather.

context.h: Port state control and the wind-port context
p: Ships calling at Port-la-Nouvelle fall under the Paris MoU, with inspections carried out by French ship safety centres. A small bulk carrier of mixed age, a tanker or a coaster all fit the targeting profile, and a recent gauging report on the hull and hold steel is useful evidence for the master if an inspector comes on board.

The Mediterranean is a SOx emission control area, so ships burning high-sulphur fuel and fitted with scrubbers work to the ECA standard on every voyage, which puts wash-water and overboard piping under closer watch. The EU Ship Recycling Regulation, EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime apply to calls here as at other EU ports. The offshore wind terminal brings a different pressure: contractors and vessel owners working on floating wind projects often ask for a documented steel condition before a charter, and gauging fits that need. The vessels themselves are often offshore support and installation ships with ballast systems and heavy deck equipment, which are checked for wastage alongside the main hull.

jobs.p: Jobs here are short and planned around a ship's berth stay and the sea state. The superintendent shares the survey due dates and the cargo plan, the agent confirms the berth and the team travels once the ship is close to arrival. Ultrasonic thickness gauging at Port-la-Nouvelle typically covers: The agent also confirms whether the wind platform quay is free, because support vessels there change often.
list: Hold frame, tank top and hopper tank gauging on a handysize bulker after discharging fertiliser.
Ballast tank, deck and bulwark readings on a tug or installation support vessel waiting at the wind platform.
Ballast tank and cofferdam gauging on a small product tanker at a liquid bulk berth.
Hatch cover and coaming readings on a coaster that carries grain in the harvest season.
Pre-docking steel estimate for a ship about to sail for a Marseille, La Ciotat or Barcelona yard.

logistics: The nearest international airports are Perpignan-Rivesaltes and Béziers-Cap d'Agde, with Montpellier and Toulouse as larger alternatives. Port-la-Nouvelle is reached by road, and the ship's agent arranges gate passes and any launch for ships waiting outside. France is in the Schengen area, so every technician needs a Schengen visa from India before travelling. We ask for the expected berth as early as possible, because visa timing and the sea state decide the earliest start. The port is small, so hotel and transfer arrangements are made early.
vessels: Offshore wind installation and support vessels

faqs.q: Can offshore wind support vessels be gauged at Port-la-Nouvelle?
faqs.a: Yes. Tugs, towing vessels and support ships lie at the wind platform between tasks, which gives time for hull, deck and ballast tank gauging. We agree the spaces with the technical manager and report by location, so wastage on heavy deck equipment foundations and ballast tanks is easy to follow.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock at Port-la-Nouvelle?
faqs.a: The port has small slipways and quayside repair suited to fishing craft and workboats, not larger merchant ships. Steel renewal on merchant ships is normally done in Marseille, La Ciotat or Barcelona. Gauging here gives readings before the voyage so the owner can scope the yard programme.

faqs.q: Can gauging happen while grain is being loaded?
faqs.a: Not in the holds being loaded. Ballast tanks, voids and deck structure can sometimes be gauged during loading if the ship releases them and the terminal permits entry. For hold structure we work between discharge and loading, when the holds are empty and swept.

faqs.q: How does the tramontane affect planning?
faqs.a: Strong north-westerly wind can delay pilots, stop launch transfers and make quay work uncomfortable. We keep a weather allowance in the plan, work alongside where possible and keep internal tank work for the windiest periods once the team is on board.

faqs.q: What must the ship provide before tanks are entered?
faqs.a: Each tank needs a gas-free certificate and an enclosed-space entry permit, with a rescue plan on deck and ventilation running throughout the work. The terminal may add its own permit when the ship is alongside. The superintendent sends the list of spaces and their sequence before the team arrives, so entry can start without delay once the ship is secure.
